![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14155852/assets/23d22833ae89d7ed3f1c34a07f039031d77223350f0b23d17c6843f67f05668c.png)

The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given above. Find ${h}^{′}(2)$ where $h(x)=2f(x)-5g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
The addition and constant multiple rules for derivatives give

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=2{f}^{′}(x)-5{g}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(2)=2{f}^{′}(2)-5{g}^{′}(2).
$$

Also, notice that $x=2$ corresponds to 

- the interval $x\in (1,3)$ for the function $f,$ and

- the interval $x\in (1,3)$ for the function $g,$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14155852/assets/1de80fcae8f07412e788df9ef202b15f5cdcf9fe8ca9a994abd8b1acd789359f.png)

- The slope of $y=f(x)$ is constant on $x\in (1,3)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δf}{Δx}=\frac{2-1}{3-1}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(2)=\frac{1}{2}.$

- The slope of $y=g(x)$ is constant on $x\in (1,3)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δg}{Δx}=\frac{-2-2}{3-1}=-2.
$$

Therefore, ${g}^{′}(2)=-2.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(2) & =2{f}^{′}(2)-5{g}^{′}(2) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}-5\cdot (-2) \\  & =11.\end{aligned}
$$
